page: Microsoft Azure D96pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz on the ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture. It features 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, backed by 128 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance lacks bundled local storage and includes zero integrated GPUs, relying on remote network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance due to the 96 independent physical execution cores. The platform achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang software compilation. High memory throughput is confirmed by top-tier uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 464 GB/sec for reads and 205 GB/sec for writes. Single-core execution in Geekbench and stress-ng falls within the average middle tier, reflecting standard per-core ARM Neoverse-N2 throughput rather than extreme burst frequencies.

With its 1:2 memory configuration, the instance trades per-core memory volume for dense, parallelized compute capacity. The dedicated single-threaded core structure avoids hyper-threading contention, translating into top-tier operational metrics in Redis key-value workloads and high-throughput static web serving. The absence of local disk devices requires provisioning remote persistent storage for stateful workloads.

The D96pls_v6 is suited for horizontally scaled multithreaded applications, microservices compilation clusters, distributed key-value caches, and parallel batch data processing that do not require high per-core RAM allocations or attached GPU acceleration.
description: Microsoft Azure D96pls_v6 is a high-density, ARM-based cloud instance powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Operating without hardware simultaneous multithreading, it pairs 96 vCPUs with 192.0 GB of RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per core alongside a 128 MB L3 cache. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier multi-threaded compute capability and high memory bandwidth, achieving exceptional results in Clang software compilation, static web serving throughput, and Redis operational benchmarks. In contrast, single-core compute performance remains in the average tier. With its 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the D96pls_v6 provides high compute density, making it effective for parallel software compilation, containerized microservices, batch processing, and high-throughput key-value storage systems.
